lessons.title: Parts of a computer and starting up
lessons.html:
What is a personal computer?

A personal computer (PC) is a machine that helps you write, calculate, store information and communicate. Many farms use computers for wage records, stock control, spray records, animal records and email. A laptop is a PC that you can carry.

Hardware: the parts you can touch

PartWhat it does
Monitor (screen)Shows the information
KeyboardTypes letters and numbers
Mouse or touchpadMoves the pointer and clicks on things
System unit / CPUThe box with the processor that does the work
Hard driveStores files when the power is off
PrinterPrints documents on paper
USB flash driveSmall portable storage

Software: the programs

  • The operating system, such as Windows, runs the computer.
  • Applications do jobs: a word processor for letters, a spreadsheet for numbers, a web browser for the internet, email programs and farm management software.

Starting and shutting down

  1. Check that cables are plugged in safely and are not damaged.
  2. Press the power button. Wait for the computer to start.
  3. Log in with your username and password.
  4. When you finish, save your work, close the programs, and use Start then Shut down. Do not just pull out the plug, as you can lose work and damage files.

Using the mouse

Click once to select, double-click to open, right-click to see more options, and click-and-drag to move something. The scroll wheel moves the page up and down.

Safe and healthy use

Keep food and drinks away from the keyboard. Do not use the computer with wet hands. Sit up straight with the screen at eye level, and rest your eyes every so often by looking away from the screen.

lessons.title: Working with files, printing and staying safe
lessons.html:
Files and folders

Everything you save on a computer is a file: a letter, a spreadsheet, a photo. Files are kept in folders, like papers in a filing cabinet. Use clear names, for example Spray records March 2026, not Document1.

Basic file tasks

  1. Create a new document in the program, for example File then New.
  2. Save it: File then Save As, choose the folder, type a name, click Save. Save often while you work; Ctrl+S is the shortcut.
  3. Open a file by double-clicking it in File Explorer.
  4. Copy and move: right-click a file and choose Copy or Cut, go to the new folder, right-click and Paste.
  5. Delete: select and press Delete. Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin and can be restored until it is emptied.

Useful keyboard shortcuts

KeysAction
Ctrl + CCopy
Ctrl + VPaste
Ctrl + ZUndo
Ctrl + PPrint

Printing

Choose File then Print. Check the printer name, the number of copies and which pages to print. Use Print Preview first to avoid wasting paper. If the printer jams, switch it off before you open it and pull the paper out gently.

Backups

Computers can break or be stolen. Keep a backup copy of important files on a flash drive, external drive or approved cloud storage, as your farm's rules say.

Staying safe

  • Use a strong password and never share it. Lock the screen (Windows key + L) when you walk away.
  • Do not open email attachments or links from people you do not know. They can carry viruses or scams.
  • Keep the antivirus program up to date.
  • Only install software that your supervisor or IT person has approved.
  • Personal information of workers must be protected. South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) requires this.

Key points

  • Hardware is the parts you can touch; software is the programs.
  • Shut down properly, do not just pull the plug.
  • Save often and use clear file and folder names.
  • Keep backups of important files.
  • Protect your password and do not open unknown attachments or links.
